osaka_spys_oasis_namba.gf_detail: The shop describes itself as serving gluten-free food and drinks, and explains on its site that it does not use gluten (「グルテンは使わないんです」). Tabelog's introduction says "completely gluten-free dishes and drinks", and a September 2026 reviewer reports "all products are 100% gluten-free", with no dairy or white sugar. Gluten-free drinks are served even at the bar, for example a GF Red Eye. Tabelog notes allergy information is available. The shop's stated reason is health rather than celiac safety, and no cross-contact controls are described, so confirm if you are celiac.
osaka_spys_oasis_namba.vegan_detail: A separate vegan-and-gluten-free curry line on the official menu: root-vegetable curry, soy-mince and red-pepper salsa curry, and a pumpkin, banana, mango, corn and chickpea curry (¥1,700 each, ¥1,800 for two, ¥1,900 for three), with vegan toppings. The house three-curry set contains chicken, pork and mackerel, and the soup is made with chicken.
osaka_spys_oasis_namba.hours_raw: Mon–Wed, Fri–Sat: lunch 11:30–15:00, bar 18:00–24:00 (one-drink minimum); Sun and holidays 11:30–15:00 and 17:00–22:00; closed Thursdays; changes on social media (official site). Online booking only, no phone reservations (official site).
osaka_spys_oasis_namba.notes: [Curry · gluten-free yakuzen spice curry by Dotonbori] A 14-seat curry café and evening bar run on a "food as medicine" concept by a yakuzen (medicinal-cooking) specialist. Everything is gluten-free by the shop's own account. The signature is three curries to mix: a soy-milk, onion, tomato and ginger chicken-breast curry; a black-sesame and red-miso pork-and-hijiki keema; and a mackerel and lotus-root "green Popeye" curry. Each is tangy and spiced, and they come together into one flavour when mixed. They sit over basmati and 15-grain rice (Simple ¥1,600; Standard ¥2,000 with soup, salad and toppings). A separate vegan line covers root-vegetable, soy-mince salsa and tropical chickpea curries. At night it becomes a bar with GF drinks, natural wine and tapas. English menu; book online.

chef_bio.background: Official site: yakuzen spice curry made by a yakuzen meister (薬膳マイスター), on the principle 医食同源 ("food and medicine share one source").
chef_bio.philosophy: 「医食同源のコンセプトの元、栄養価はもちろん、身体に優しい食材を厳選」 (official site).

anecdotes.text: 「スパイスオアシスは、薬膳マイスターが作る薬膳スパイスカレーとグルテンフリーのドリンクとフードが楽しめるお店です」 (official site).
"All products are 100% gluten-free, with no dairy, white sugar, or chemical seasonings and additives." — September 2026.

osaka_old_cairo_cafe.gf_detail: Ask. Koshari contains macaroni and hummus comes with pita, but rice plates and grilled skewers may suit; nothing is described as gluten-free.
osaka_old_cairo_cafe.vegan_detail: Tabelog lists vegan, vegetarian and halal options. The Egyptian menu includes koshari (rice, macaroni and lentils with tomato sauce and fried onion), ta'ameya falafel, hummus with pita and molokhia soup. None is described as vegan in reviews, so ask about ghee, stock and dairy.
osaka_old_cairo_cafe.hours_raw: Daily 12:00–17:00 (L.O. 16:30) and 18:00–1:00 (L.O. 0:30), but opening days, closures and private events are posted on Instagram; one reviewer found it closed several times (September 2026). QR payment only. Lunch non-smoking; dinner smoking allowed (shisha) (Tabelog).
osaka_old_cairo_cafe.notes: [Middle Eastern · an Egyptian café and shisha bar in Amemura] A moody, Egyptian-styled café on the 3rd floor of a building in Amerikamura that serves lunch and runs as a shisha bar at night, with occasional dance shows. Staff explain the dishes and share stories about Egypt. Order koshari, the national dish of rice, macaroni and lentils in tomato sauce under crisp fried onions, with garlic vinegar and chili oil to season. There's also ta'ameya (Egyptian falafel), hummus with pita, a rich, garlicky molokhia soup, and shish tawook chicken plates (about ¥1,600–1,800). Finish with baklava or kahk and hibiscus juice or mint tea. Tabelog lists vegan, vegetarian and halal options. Opening days vary, so check Instagram or book. On event nights, food can take an hour.

chef_bio.background: An Egyptian restaurant and shisha café; operating days announced on Instagram (Tabelog remarks). No source names the operator.

anecdotes.text: "I ordered koshari, Egypt's national dish… It consists of rice, macaroni, and lentils topped with tomato sauce. The generous amount of crispy fried onions added a delightful crunch." — September 2026.

"We ordered: Koshari, Hummus with Pita Bread, Molokhia Soup, Ta'ameya Falafel, Kahk, Baklava, Hibiscus Juice… The staff carefully explained each dish and shared interesting facts about Egypt." — August 2026.

osaka_creperie_alcyon_namba.gf_detail: Ask. Savoury galettes are traditionally buckwheat, but no source says these are 100% buckwheat or wheat-free; the sweet crêpes use French wheat flour (Tabelog).
osaka_creperie_alcyon_namba.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog lists "vegetarian options", but crêpes and galettes use Échiré butter, eggs and cheese; no vegetarian dish is described.
osaka_creperie_alcyon_namba.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:30–21:30; Sat, Sun and holidays 11:00–21:30; L.O. 20:30. Lunch 11:30–15:00 (weekends 11:00–17:00), café and takeout to 20:30 (Tabelog). Cash only. No reservations for more than four. Steep stairs.
osaka_creperie_alcyon_namba.notes: [Sweets · Namba's famous crêpes and galettes] A 50-seat French crêperie up steep stairs just south of Dotonbori, named to Tabelog's Sweets WEST "100" in 2023 and 2026, with a takeout line downstairs. The crêpes, made with French flour, Échiré butter and salt, are crisp at the edge and chewy inside. The plain Échiré butter and sugar is the one regulars call the best they've had. At lunch, try a daily galette from the blackboard, say beef stew over mashed potato and cheese, or tandoori chicken, in the crêperie lunch (¥2,200, October 2026). There's also a milk-jam crêpe set with vanilla gelato (¥1,480), quiche and Mont Blanc. The takeout queue is about 10 minutes. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Selected for Tabelog Sweets WEST "100" 2023 and 2026; Tabelog introduction: French flour, Échiré butter and salt.

anecdotes.text: "Both were perfectly crispy and fragrant, and the batter itself was outstanding! The galette had beef stew underneath, with mashed potatoes and cheese hidden between the layers." — October 2026, crêperie lunch ¥2,200, cash only.
"I had a crepe with Échiré butter and sugar. The takeout line took about 10 minutes… The outside was crispy while the inside was chewy and moist." — October 2026.

osaka_green_bar_shinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog lists "vegetarian options". The green smoothie is komatsuna, apple and banana (May 2024), but milk and yoghurt bases are not ruled out.
osaka_green_bar_shinsaibashi.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–21:00 (L.O. 20:30), closed only on 1 January (Tabelog). Order at the kiosk; small eat-in space next door. Cards, e-money and QR accepted.
osaka_green_bar_shinsaibashi.notes: [Café · a healthy smoothie stand on Shinsaibashi-suji] A small café stand run by the apparel brand Urban Research, beside its store on the Shinsaibashi-suji arcade, with a tucked-away eat-in corner and a terrace. Smoothies are made to order from fresh vegetables and fruit, like the smooth green komatsuna, apple and banana, or a seasonal peach. There are also matcha crêpes with shiratama (¥700), lattes and bagels for a light bite. Service at the kiosk can be brisk when it's busy with overseas visitors.

chef_bio.background: Operated by the apparel company Urban Research (November 2023 review).

anecdotes.text: "I found a 'Green Smoothie' made with komatsuna (Japanese mustard spinach), apple, and banana… It was pleasantly smooth without any gritty texture." — May 2024.

osaka_minmin_namba_walk.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat-wrapper gyoza, noodles, soy-based Chinese sauces.
osaka_minmin_namba_walk.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pork gyoza, kara-age, Genghis Khan lamb, mapo tofu with meat.
osaka_minmin_namba_walk.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–22:00 (L.O. 21:30); closed the third Wednesday of odd-numbered months (Tabelog). Cash only (no cards or e-money, per Tabelog). Smartphone ordering; free Wi-Fi.
osaka_minmin_namba_walk.notes: [Gyoza · Minmin under Namba] Minmin's 43-seat branch in the Namba Walk underground mall, busy with office workers at lunch and handy in the rain. The light, distinctive gyoza (¥450) are the reason to come. Set meals are cheap: Genghis Khan lamb and onions with rice, pickles and egg soup (¥880), clay-pot mapo tofu, crisp kara-age. À la carte, fried rice is ¥770 and stir-fried squid with garlic chives ¥820 (September 2026). Prices hold to the menu, with no extras. Service is quiet to curt, and you order on your phone. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Minmin (minminhonten.com) opened its first shop in Sennichimae in 1953 (Tabelog listing).

"I ordered the Genghis Khan Set Meal for JPY 880, which comes with rice, pickled mustard greens, and egg soup." — September 2026.

osaka_kamukura_namba_walk.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; gyoza, fried rice.
osaka_kamukura_namba_walk.vegan_detail: Not vegan as far as sources show: the broth base is not described, and sets pair the ramen with gyoza and kara-age. Ask.
osaka_kamukura_namba_walk.hours_raw: Daily 10:00–22:00 (L.O. 21:30) (Tabelog). Tablet ordering at the table. Cards, e-money and QR accepted.
osaka_kamukura_namba_walk.notes: [Ramen · Kamukura in the Namba Walk mall] A roomy Kamukura in the Namba Walk underground mall, since 2024, with tables that suit solo diners and tablet ordering. The broth is the chain's soy-based soup, light but deep with the sweetness of napa cabbage. The vegetable-packed ramen is the regulars' choice, topped up with the garlic chives at the counter. Autumn 2026 brought a limited hot-and-sour ramen, lighter than the usual thick suan-la, just right for some and refreshing for others. A ramen, gyoza, fried rice and beer set makes a hearty lunch.

chef_bio.background: Kamukura chain; Namba Walk shop page (walk.osaka-chikagai.jp).

anecdotes.text: "Doutonbori KAMUKURA's ramen features a light yet rich broth that highlights the sweetness of napa cabbage… The soy sauce-based soup, infused with the umami of the cabbage, is both gentle and deeply flavorful." — October 2026.
"It feels like a light hot and sour soup poured over a delicious regular ramen, resulting in a thinner broth." — October 2026, limited hot-and-sour ramen.

osaka_yakitori_kamameshi_nakamoto.gf_detail: Ask. Sources give no allergen information; the seasoning of the yakitori and kamameshi is not described, and there are fried dishes.
osaka_yakitori_kamameshi_nakamoto.vegan_detail: Not vegan: chicken-centred menu; kamameshi with chicken soboro. There is a grilled-vegetable plate, but its seasoning is not described.
osaka_yakitori_kamameshi_nakamoto.hours_raw: Daily 17:00–4:00 (food L.O. 3:00, drinks 3:30), open year-round (Tabelog). LINE / mobile ordering. Smoking only on the terrace (Tabelog). Order the kamameshi early; it is cooked to order. 2-hour limit at busy times (Tabelog). Cards and QR accepted; no e-money.
osaka_yakitori_kamameshi_nakamoto.notes: [Yakitori · Kyushu-style yakitori and kamameshi by Namba station] A red-lantern izakaya in a back alley by Namba Station, open from 5 pm to 4 am, part of the SASAYA group. Charcoal-grilled Kyushu-style yakitori comes as shareable pieces rather than skewers: an assorted three kinds is ¥1,320 (April 2026), alongside grilled vegetables (¥1,078) and fried mehikari (¥858). Finish with kamameshi, rice cooked to order in an iron pot, like the chicken soboro and burdock, so order it early. Ordering is by LINE. The upstairs can get smoky from the grill, and there's a pleasant terrace. Note the name: Tabelog lists it as Nakamoto, while several 2026 reviews call it "Yakitori to Kamameshi Gotchin".

chef_bio.origin: Opened 4 April 2025 (Tabelog), on the former site of a Thai street-food stall (April 2026 review)
chef_bio.background: A SASAYA-group shop (April 2026 review). Reviewers from January–August 2026 call it "Yakitori to Kamameshi Gotchin"; Tabelog lists it as Nakamoto.

anecdotes.text: "The grilled yakitori is served as individual pieces rather than skewers. You can order the Assorted Yakitori (3 types) for JPY 1,320, tax included, with orders available through LINE registration." — April 2026.
"The 'Chicken Soboro and Burdock Kamameshi' I had this time featured fluffy rice topped with sweet and savory chicken soboro and crunchy burdock." — January 2026.

osaka_ichiban_malatang_nipponbashi.gf_detail: Ask. You choose your own ingredients (vegetables such as broccoli), but what goes into the beef-bone broth and the other soups is not described; check any noodles or processed items for wheat.
osaka_ichiban_malatang_nipponbashi.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–24:00 (Tabelog). Cards and QR accepted. A free drink with orders over ¥1,000 (2026).
osaka_ichiban_malatang_nipponbashi.notes: [Chinese · malatang with a beef-bone white broth in Nippombashi] A clean, 20-seat malatang shop a few minutes from Nippombashi, relaxed enough when reviewers came that you can take your time at the ingredient case. The difference is the broth: beef bone, and the original white version is rich enough at zero spice to taste like ramen soup. Vegetables soaked in it, broccoli especially, are the reviewers' pick. Spice runs from 0 up to a numbing level 3 at least, and chili oil comes on the side. One mala fan ranks it third of 19 places tried. Spend over ¥1,000, as most do, and a can from the fridge is free. The aroma inside takes a minute to get used to.

anecdotes.text: "I went for the original flavor white broth. It was almost non-spicy, allowing me to fully enjoy the restaurant's tasty soup… I highly recommend the broccoli. I'm also happy that drinks are complimentary." — August 2026.
"I've tried various mala tang dishes (ranking 3rd out of 19 places) and this one is in my top three!… the spiciness level 3 was just perfect for me." — October 2026.
